map.Selling only to other businesses in bulk: Selling goods to other businesses in large wholesale lots
map.Selling only through one physical store: Opening many stores in different cities under one brand name
map.Using several unrelated channels that do: Using several separate channels that each keep their own records

ww.Selling goods to other businesses in lar: Selling in bulk to other businesses is wholesale or business-to-business trade. Omnichannel is a retail approach that links the channels customers use to shop.
ww.Opening many stores in different cities: Adding more stores expands locations but keeps one channel. Omnichannel links different channels, such as stores, apps and websites, into one connected experience.
ww.Using several separate channels that eac: Separate channels with their own records describe multichannel retailing. Omnichannel connects them so inventory, accounts and order history are shared across channels.

map.Higher prices for every customer in the: Automatic price cuts on slow selling products
map.Fewer products offered to customers in e: Reduced shoplifting by tracking customers in the store

ww.Automatic price cuts on slow selling pro: Scanning records sales and does not set prices. Markdowns are management decisions, while the main gain from scanning is current stock data.
ww.Reduced shoplifting by tracking customer: Scanning at checkout records sales and does not watch customers. Theft is handled by security tools and physical counts, while scans keep stock records current.

map.A government-run store that sells goods: A cooperative owned by its customers who share the profits
map.A store that sells only used goods bough: A chain store owned and run directly by the producer's head office

ww.A cooperative owned by its customers who: A store owned by its customer members is a consumer cooperative. Franchisees are independent owners licensed to use a brand and follow its system.
ww.A chain store owned and run directly by: A store the producer owns and runs itself is a company-owned outlet. A franchise is run by an independent owner who pays fees to use the brand.

map.Using every possible outlet that is open: Placing the product in as many stores as will stock it
map.Using only one outlet in a region, so th: Giving one retailer the sole right to sell in a region
map.Using no outlets at all, and selling onl: Selling directly to buyers through a website and catalog

ww.Placing the product in as many stores as: Getting the product into as many stores as possible is intensive distribution. Selective distribution picks a limited group of outlets that suit the brand.
ww.Giving one retailer the sole right to se: Granting one retailer a region's sales rights is exclusive distribution. Selective distribution works with several carefully chosen outlets instead of a single one.
ww.Selling directly to buyers through a web: Selling direct to buyers through a website or catalog skips retail outlets. Selective distribution still sells through a chosen group of stores.

map.Samples are always more accurate than an: Samples include more people than a census would
map.Samples avoid the need to ask any questi: Samples let firms skip analyzing the data they collect

ww.Samples include more people than a censu: A census covers the whole population, so a sample is smaller, not larger. Samples are used because they save time and money.
ww.Samples let firms skip analyzing the dat: Sample data still has to be analyzed to find results. Samples cut cost and time by studying fewer people, not by skipping analysis.

map.Data that is secret and kept inside one: Data a company gathers from its own sales and customer records
map.Data collected by one company for its ow: Data gathered by a government agency and posted for public use

ww.Data a company gathers from its own sale: Data from a company's own sales records is internal data. Syndicated data is gathered by an outside research firm and sold to many clients.
ww.Data gathered by a government agency and: Government data released to the public is a free secondary source. Syndicated data is gathered by a private research firm and sold to paying clients.

map.Inflation completely for every investor: The rate of inflation in the economy
map.Every kind of risk that investors face: The fees charged by fund managers

ww.The rate of inflation in the economy: Inflation affects the buying power of money across the economy, and owning many investments does not change it. Diversification reduces the risk tied to one holding.
ww.The fees charged by fund managers: Fees are set by funds and brokers and do not shrink because you own more holdings. Diversification spreads out the loss risk tied to one investment.

map.Investments never lose any value: Investment accounts pay a fixed yearly rate
map.Fees are always zero at the start: Beginners receive higher returns than older investors

ww.Investment accounts pay a fixed yearly r: Most investments earn varying returns that rise and fall, so no fixed rate is paid. Starting early helps because growth has more years to compound.
ww.Beginners receive higher returns than ol: Returns depend on the investments chosen, not on the investor's age. Starting early helps because growth has more years to compound.

map.Paying only the minimum amount due each: Paying the minimum plus a small extra amount
map.Skipping a payment every now and then to: Paying the balance a few days after the due date

ww.Paying the minimum plus a small extra am: Paying slightly above the minimum still leaves a balance, so interest keeps accruing on it. Paying in full by the due date is what avoids interest.
ww.Paying the balance a few days after the: Paying after the due date brings a late fee and can end the grace period, so interest is charged. The balance must be paid in full on time.

map.A loan guaranteed only by the borrower's: A loan approved on the borrower's good credit score and income
map.A loan that charges no interest and requ: A loan with a fixed interest rate that stays the same for its term

ww.A loan approved on the borrower's good c: A loan approved on credit and income without pledged property is unsecured. A secured loan is backed by collateral the lender can claim after a default.
ww.A loan with a fixed interest rate that s: A fixed rate describes how interest is set, not what secures the loan. A secured loan is defined by collateral the lender can claim if the borrower defaults.

map.A savings plan that guarantees a return: A retirement account that grows through investments chosen by the owner
map.A tax refund paid by the government each: A government benefit that replaces wages after a job loss

ww.A retirement account that grows through: A retirement account is an investment product the owner funds and manages. Insurance transfers the risk of loss to an insurer in return for premiums.
ww.A government benefit that replaces wages: Unemployment benefits replace income after a job loss and are paid by the state. Insurance is a contract where premiums buy protection against covered losses.

map.Interest earned only on the original dep: Interest calculated on the starting deposit alone
map.Interest charged only once at the start: A rate that falls as the balance grows

ww.Interest calculated on the starting depo: Interest on the starting deposit alone is simple interest. Compound interest also earns interest on interest already added, so the balance grows faster.
ww.A rate that falls as the balance grows: Compound interest does not lower the rate as the balance grows. It adds earned interest to the balance, so later interest is calculated on a larger amount.

map.Contractors always earn more than employ: Contractors get paid vacation but employees do not
map.Employees always get to choose their own: Contractors receive a W-2 and employees receive a 1099

ww.Contractors get paid vacation but employ: Paid vacation is usually an employee benefit, while contractors typically get none. The main difference is that employers withhold tax for employees and contractors handle their own.
ww.Contractors receive a W-2 and employees: It is reversed: employees receive a W-2 and contractors receive a 1099. The key difference is who handles the taxes on the pay.

map.The pay that applies to workers who rece: The average hourly pay for workers in a given industry
map.The pay that applies to managers and exe: The extra pay an employer must give for overtime hours

ww.The average hourly pay for workers in a: An average wage describes typical pay across a field. Minimum wage is the legal floor, which employers can pay more than but not less than.
ww.The extra pay an employer must give for: Overtime pay is a premium for hours past the weekly limit. Minimum wage is the lowest hourly pay allowed for covered workers.

map.Waiting a week before buying anything at: Waiting a week to compare options before buying
map.Buying only what is on a planned list at: Buying a needed item after reading reviews
map.Comparing prices before buying anything: Paying with cash to stay within a budget

ww.Waiting a week to compare options before: Waiting and comparing is a planned approach that guards against impulse buying. Impulse buying is an unplanned purchase made on a sudden urge.
ww.Buying a needed item after reading revie: Buying after research is a planned purchase. Impulse buying happens without planning, driven by a sudden urge, display or sale.
ww.Paying with cash to stay within a budget: Paying cash to stay in budget is a spending control. Impulse buying is an unplanned purchase made on a sudden urge.

map.Interest that is paid only when a person: Interest paid as a flat fee once a year by the bank
map.Interest that is earned only on the orig: Interest that is calculated on the starting deposit alone

ww.Interest paid as a flat fee once a year: Compound interest is not a flat yearly fee. It is added to the balance on a schedule, and later interest is earned on that larger balance.
ww.Interest that is calculated on the start: Interest on the starting deposit alone is simple interest. Compound interest also earns interest on previous interest, so it grows faster over time.

map.Banks always pay younger savers higher r: Taxes on savings are lower for younger savers
map.You can spend all of your income right a: You can skip making a budget in later years
map.You will never need to save any money ag: Your deposits are protected from inflation as years pass

ww.Taxes on savings are lower for younger s: Tax on interest depends on income and tax rules, not on the saver's age. Starting early helps because compound interest has more years to build.
ww.You can skip making a budget in later ye: Saving early does not remove the need to budget later. The real advantage is that compound interest has more time to build the balance.
ww.Your deposits are protected from inflati: Deposits can lose buying power when inflation outpaces the interest earned. The real advantage of starting early is more time for compound interest to work.

map.To buy individual stocks only, with no o: To save for a first home with tax advantages
map.To save for family vacations only, and f: To build a general emergency fund with tax advantages

ww.To save for a first home with tax advant: A 529 plan is built for education costs. Using it for a home purchase is not a qualified expense and can bring taxes and penalties.
ww.To build a general emergency fund with t: A 529 plan is meant for qualified education costs. Emergency savings belong in a flexible account, since non education withdrawals from a 529 can bring taxes and penalties.

map.A card whose balance never needs to be r: A card that earns cash back on grocery purchases
map.A card that is issued only to businesses: A card that comes with a lower rate for a year

ww.A card that earns cash back on grocery p: Cash back is a rewards feature on many cards. A secured card is defined by the cash deposit that backs its credit limit.
ww.A card that comes with a lower rate for: A temporary low rate describes an introductory offer. A secured card is defined by the cash deposit that backs the credit limit.

map.A loan guaranteed by the borrower's sign: A loan approved by the lender based on your credit score
map.A loan that carries no repayment require: A loan with a fixed rate and equal monthly payments

ww.A loan approved by the lender based on y: A loan approved on credit score alone is unsecured. A secured loan is tied to pledged property the lender can take if you default.
ww.A loan with a fixed rate and equal month: A fixed rate and equal payments describe how a loan is repaid. A secured loan is defined by collateral the lender can claim if you default.

ww.Once in two years: Federal law allows a free report from each bureau at least once a year, so a two year wait is longer than needed. Yearly checks help catch errors early.
ww.Once per five years: Free reports are available at least yearly, so a five year gap would leave errors or identity theft unnoticed for far too long.
ww.Once per decade: A ten year gap is much longer than the yearly access federal law provides, and it would let errors or fraud go unnoticed.

map.Cancels all of the cards that you hold t: Lowers the interest rates on your current cards
map.Erases all of the debts that you owe to: Removes late payments from your credit report

ww.Lowers the interest rates on your curren: A freeze restricts access to your credit report and does not change card rates. Rates are set by the issuer under your account terms.
ww.Removes late payments from your credit r: A freeze does not edit your history, so late payments stay on the report. It blocks lenders from viewing the report for new credit.

map.Close every account that you have open: Open many new cards in a short time
map.Max out your cards every single month: Carry a balance to show lenders you use credit

ww.Open many new cards in a short time: Many new applications create hard inquiries and lower your average account age, which can hurt a score. Steady on-time payments and low balances build credit.
ww.Carry a balance to show lenders you use: Carrying a balance adds interest cost without raising a score. Paying on time and keeping balances low builds a good history.

map.Only people who never work at any job: People who rent and own few possessions
map.No one at all, ever, in any situation: People who want protection for their car

ww.People who rent and own few possessions: Renting or owning few things is not a reason for life insurance. It protects dependents who would lose income, not property.
ww.People who want protection for their car: Protection for a car comes from auto insurance. Life insurance replaces income for dependents who would struggle financially after a death.

map.Coverage for car accidents and repairs o: Coverage for car accidents and medical bills
map.Coverage that is meant for renters only: Coverage for tenants' belongings in a rented apartment

ww.Coverage for car accidents and medical b: Car accidents are covered by auto insurance, a separate policy. Homeowners insurance protects the house, belongings and liability on the property.
ww.Coverage for tenants' belongings in a re: That describes renters insurance for tenants. Homeowners insurance covers owners' houses, belongings and liability, and mortgage lenders often require it.

map.The owner is not allowed to file any cla: The home was too old to qualify for coverage
map.Floods are always covered in standard po: Floods are covered once the deductible is doubled

ww.The home was too old to qualify for cove: Standard policies exclude flood damage regardless of the home's age. Flood coverage must be bought separately, often through the National Flood Insurance Program.
ww.Floods are covered once the deductible i: Standard policies exclude flood damage, and a higher deductible does not change that. Separate flood insurance is needed to cover it.

map.A fund guaranteed to never lose any of y: A fund that pays a fixed rate of interest on deposits
map.A fund that holds only one stock at a ti: A fund that employers set up to pay employee pensions

ww.A fund that pays a fixed rate of interes: A fund that pays fixed interest describes a bond or savings product. An index fund holds the securities in a market index and its value rises and falls.
ww.A fund that employers set up to pay empl: A pension fund is set up by an employer to pay retirement benefits. An index fund is an investment fund that tracks a market index.

map.Higher returns always come with no risk: Higher potential returns usually come with lower risk
map.Low risk always guarantees high returns: Risk affects an investment's fees but not its returns

ww.Higher potential returns usually come wi: It reverses the relationship. Investors accept more risk in exchange for the chance of higher returns, as with stocks compared with savings accounts.
ww.Risk affects an investment's fees but no: Risk is linked to expected returns because investors demand more reward for taking more uncertainty. Fees are a separate cost.

map.A loan that is made to retired people on: A loan used to buy a home
map.An insurance policy for retirees only: A pension paid by an employer
map.A government tax form filed by retirees: A federal program that pays monthly benefits

ww.A loan used to buy a home: A home loan is a mortgage. An IRA is an individual retirement account for saving, not a loan.
ww.A pension paid by an employer: A pension is an employer-funded retirement benefit. An IRA is a personal account the individual opens and funds, with tax advantages.
ww.A federal program that pays monthly bene: Social Security pays monthly benefits funded through payroll taxes. An IRA is a personal retirement savings account with its own tax advantages.

map.It pays a guaranteed return of ten perce: Withdrawals must start at age 59 and a half
map.Withdrawals are always free of any rules: The government matches the contributions you make

ww.Withdrawals must start at age 59 and a h: Roth IRAs have no required withdrawals during the owner's life. Age 59 and a half is when earnings can be withdrawn tax-free if the account is five years old.
ww.The government matches the contributions: The government does not match Roth IRA contributions; employers may match 401(k) contributions. A Roth works with after-tax contributions and tax-free qualified withdrawals.

map.Fees are lower for all of the early inve: Brokers pay early investors a yearly bonus
map.Taxes disappear for early investors in e: Tax rates on gains drop when you start young
map.Early investors never lose any money at: Markets rise steadily in the first years of investing

ww.Brokers pay early investors a yearly bon: Brokers do not pay bonuses for starting early. The real benefit is that compounding has more years to build on earnings.
ww.Tax rates on gains drop when you start y: Tax rates depend on income, holding period and account type, not on when you began investing. Starting early helps because compounding has more time to work.
ww.Markets rise steadily in the first years: Markets move up and down in any period, including early years. Starting early helps by giving compounding and recovery more time.

map.An account that guarantees a set rate of: A savings account that pays a fixed interest rate
map.An account that is used only for borrowi: An account that holds money for a child's education

ww.A savings account that pays a fixed inte: A savings account pays interest set by the institution. A brokerage account holds investments such as stocks and funds, whose value rises and falls.
ww.An account that holds money for a child': An education savings account such as a 529 holds money for school costs. A brokerage account is used to buy and sell investments.

map.Fees only affect investors who hold for: Fees matter for traders but not for people who buy funds
map.Fees have no effect at all on returns ov: Fees are paid by the broker and not by the investor

ww.Fees matter for traders but not for peop: Fund fees are charged on balances held in funds, so buy and hold investors pay them too. Over decades they reduce the amount that compounds.
ww.Fees are paid by the broker and not by t: Investors pay fees directly or through fund expense ratios. These costs come out of the balance and reduce the amount left to compound.

map.A single speculative bet on one company: A portfolio concentrated in one popular sector
map.Only a one-month Treasury bill held to m: A portfolio of savings accounts and CDs
map.Only cash kept hidden under a mattress a: A mix of short term bonds and cash

ww.A portfolio concentrated in one popular: Concentrating in one sector adds risk that diversification would reduce. A long horizon calls for a diversified mix, not a bet on a single area.
ww.A portfolio of savings accounts and CDs: Savings accounts and CDs are safe but earn low returns that can trail inflation over 40 years. A long horizon suits a diversified, stock weighted mix.
ww.A mix of short term bonds and cash: Short term bonds and cash protect principal but grow slowly. With 40 years to ride out downturns, a diversified, stock weighted mix offers more growth.

map.All of the money in cryptocurrency coins: Mostly stock index funds to chase higher growth
map.All of the money in a single volatile te: A portfolio of small company stocks and real estate
map.All of the money in a long-term growth f: A long term bond fund with changing prices

ww.Mostly stock index funds to chase higher: Stock funds can fall sharply in a year, and a one year goal leaves no time to recover. Safe, liquid options protect the principal.
ww.A portfolio of small company stocks and: Small company stocks and real estate can lose value and may be hard to sell fast. A one year goal calls for safety and easy access.
ww.A long term bond fund with changing pric: Long term bond funds change in price when rates move and can lose value over one year. Savings accounts or CDs protect principal for short goals.

map.Lower rates always earn you more money e: A higher rate means the account is safer to use
map.Rates do not affect how much you earn at: Rates matter for loans but not for savings accounts

ww.A higher rate means the account is safer: A rate shows the interest paid, not how safe the account is. Safety depends on deposit insurance. Comparing rates helps because a higher rate earns more.
ww.Rates matter for loans but not for savin: Savings rates directly set how much interest you earn, just as loan rates set what you pay. Comparing them shows which account pays more.

map.Never spending money on anything: Spending savings to cover regular bills
map.Borrowing money for every purchase: Relying on loans to keep up your lifestyle

ww.Spending savings to cover regular bills: Using savings to cover regular bills means spending beyond your income. Living within your means keeps spending at or below what you earn.
ww.Relying on loans to keep up your lifesty: Relying on loans to maintain a lifestyle means spending more than you earn. Living within your means keeps spending at or below income.

map.Old accounts are not counted in any cred: It triggers a late payment mark on the report
map.Closed accounts are always deleted at on: It adds a hard inquiry to the credit report

ww.It triggers a late payment mark on the r: Closing an account in good standing does not create a late payment mark. The score can drop because history shortens and utilization rises.
ww.It adds a hard inquiry to the credit rep: Closing a card does not add a hard inquiry, which comes from applying for credit. The score can fall because history shortens and utilization rises.

map.A rate that is always set at zero for th: A rate that the borrower can change by asking each month
map.A rate that never changes during the who: A rate that is locked in at approval for the full term

ww.A rate that the borrower can change by a: Borrowers cannot reset their own rate. A variable rate moves with a benchmark such as the prime rate, so the lender's terms adjust it.
ww.A rate that is locked in at approval for: A rate locked in at approval is a fixed rate, the opposite of a variable rate. A variable rate follows market benchmarks and can change your payment.

map.A regular expense that comes up every mo: A planned expense with a known price, like a vacation
map.A cost that you choose to avoid complete: A purchase that you can easily delay until next year if needed

ww.A planned expense with a known price, li: A known planned cost is best handled by budgeting and saving ahead. Insurance fits uncertain losses too large to cover from savings.
ww.A purchase that you can easily delay unt: A delayable purchase is a choice, not a loss. Insurance suits uncertain events with costs too large for savings to cover.

map.Spend all of your money on eggs and bask: Keep your money in one bank account
map.Buy only one single stock that you trust: Buy the stock of a company you trust
map.Avoid investing in anything at all, ever: Sell your investments when prices begin to fall

ww.Keep your money in one bank account: Keeping your money in one place does not spread risk. The saying advises dividing it among different investments.
ww.Buy the stock of a company you trust: Putting money into one company concentrates risk. The saying warns against that and advises spreading money across different investments.
ww.Sell your investments when prices begin: Selling when prices fall locks in losses and does not spread risk. The saying advises holding a mix of different investments.

map.It guarantees investment gains every sin: It cuts the fees charged by your fund each year
map.It lowers your income tax to zero every: It lets you borrow from the employer at no interest

ww.It cuts the fees charged by your fund ea: A match is money from the employer and does not change fund fees. Its benefit is the extra contribution added to your retirement savings.
ww.It lets you borrow from the employer at: A match is a contribution to your account, not a loan. Any loan from a 401(k) must be repaid, and the match is extra money added to your savings.

map.A market where only livestock is traded: A period when companies report weak profits and job losses
map.A period when prices never change at all: A market for stocks that trade below five dollars each

ww.A period when companies report weak prof: Weak profits and job losses describe a recession or downturn. A bull market is defined by rising stock prices and investor optimism.
ww.A market for stocks that trade below fiv: Stocks priced under five dollars are penny stocks. A bull market describes a rising market for securities, whatever their price.

map.It guarantees the same results next year: It reliably predicts next year's results
map.It is the only factor that matters: It matters more than fees, risk and goals

ww.It reliably predicts next year's results: Past returns are not a reliable forecast, since markets and conditions change. That is why ads warn that past performance does not promise future results.
ww.It matters more than fees, risk and goal: Fees, risk and goals matter at least as much as past returns. A fund's history is one piece of information among several.

map.Spending all of your savings right away: Moving the money into a checking account
map.Keeping all of your savings in cash for: Holding the money in a low rate savings account

ww.Moving the money into a checking account: Checking accounts pay little or no interest, so inflation erodes the buying power. A diversified mix that outpaces inflation protects savings better.
ww.Holding the money in a low rate savings: A low rate account usually earns less than inflation, so buying power shrinks over decades. A diversified mix that outpaces inflation protects it better.

map.Use the card only for cash advances at t: Use the card for cash advances and repay them within a week
map.Pay only the minimum amount each month o: Pay the minimum plus a little extra on the balance each month

ww.Use the card for cash advances and repay: Cash advances usually charge a fee and start accruing interest at once, with no grace period. Paying the full statement balance by the due date avoids interest.
ww.Pay the minimum plus a little extra on t: A balance carried past the due date accrues interest, even if payments exceed the minimum. Paying the full statement balance avoids interest.

map.Pay from tips and bonuses only: The hourly rate in the offer
map.Pay before any deductions at all: Pay before taxes are taken out

ww.The hourly rate in the offer: The hourly rate is the stated pay before taxes and deductions. Take-home pay is what remains after they are subtracted.
ww.Pay for extra hours worked: Pay for extra hours is still counted before taxes and deductions. Take-home pay is the amount left after they come out.
ww.Pay before taxes are taken out: Pay before taxes is gross pay. Take-home pay, also called net pay, is what remains after taxes and deductions are subtracted.

map.Guaranteed steady pay every week and mon: Paid vacation and sick leave from the platform
map.Employer-paid health insurance always at: Steady weekly pay set by an employer

ww.Paid vacation and sick leave from the pl: Gig platforms rarely provide paid leave, and that would be a benefit and not a downside. The drawbacks are changing income and limited benefits.
ww.Steady weekly pay set by an employer: Gig earnings depend on demand and available jobs, so pay is not steady. That uncertainty is the downside, along with limited benefits.

map.Education lowers taxes on all of the inc: Education moves a worker into a lower tax bracket
map.Education guarantees a job without any e: Education lets workers skip applying and interviewing

ww.Education moves a worker into a lower ta: Higher earnings usually mean higher taxes, not lower. Education raises pay because it builds skills and credentials employers value.
ww.Education lets workers skip applying and: Educated workers still apply, interview and compete for jobs. Education raises earnings by building skills and credentials that employers value.

map.A cost that is always zero every single: A cost that appears when something breaks
map.A cost that changes every single month: A cost that changes with the season

ww.A cost that appears when something break: A cost that appears when something breaks is an unplanned expense. A fixed expense is a regular cost that stays the same amount.
ww.A cost that changes with the season: A cost that shifts with the season is a variable expense, such as heating. A fixed expense stays the same amount each month.

map.A cost that never changes at all in a ye: A cost that stays level during a contract
map.A cost that is the same every single mon: A cost paid as the same amount on a loan schedule

ww.A cost that stays level during a contrac: A cost that stays level during a contract is a fixed expense, such as rent. A variable expense changes in amount from month to month.
ww.A cost paid as the same amount on a loan: Loan payments on a schedule are a fixed expense because the amount repeats. A variable expense changes in size from month to month.

map.You can spend all of your income on fun: Savings are protected from rising prices
map.You never need to save again in your lif: You can skip saving once you get a raise

ww.Savings are protected from rising prices: Savings can lose buying power if prices rise faster than interest. Starting early helps because compound interest has more time to grow.
ww.You can skip saving once you get a raise: Saving must continue as expenses and goals change, whatever your income. Starting early helps because compound interest has more time to grow.

map.A gift that never needs any repayment at: Credit you can borrow, repay and borrow again
map.A credit line with no end date at all fo: A short loan repaid from your next paycheck

ww.Credit you can borrow, repay and borrow: Borrowing and reborrowing up to a limit is revolving credit. An installment loan is repaid in fixed regular payments until the balance reaches zero.
ww.A short loan repaid from your next paych: A loan repaid from your next paycheck is a payday loan. An installment loan is repaid in fixed regular payments over a set term.

map.A loan repaid in fixed payments over set: A loan repaid in fixed monthly payments until the balance is zero
map.A loan with no interest that you never r: A loan secured by a car or house you pledge

ww.A loan repaid in fixed monthly payments: Fixed payments until the balance is zero describe an installment loan. Revolving credit can be used, repaid and used again up to a limit.
ww.A loan secured by a car or house you ple: A loan backed by pledged property is a secured loan. Revolving credit is a limit you can reuse as you repay, as with credit cards.

map.The monthly payment only, times the mont: The principal plus the first year's interest
map.The interest rate only, with no fees inc: The annual percentage rate of the loan
map.The principal only, with no interest or: The amount of the down payment

ww.The principal plus the first year's inte: Counting just the first year's interest leaves out later interest and fees. Total cost is the principal plus all interest and fees over the loan.
ww.The annual percentage rate of the loan: The APR is a yearly rate that expresses the cost of borrowing. Total cost is a dollar amount: the principal plus all interest and fees.
ww.The amount of the down payment: A down payment is the amount paid upfront and does not show what the loan costs. Total cost is the principal plus all interest and fees.

map.You can never drive the car on any publi: You must pay the full price of the car upfront
map.You always pay less overall in the long: You build equity in the car with each payment

ww.You must pay the full price of the car u: Leases usually need lower upfront payments than a purchase. The drawbacks are no ownership and mileage limits, with fees if you go over.
ww.You build equity in the car with each pa: Lease payments do not build equity because the lessor holds title. Buying builds ownership, while leasing leaves you with mileage limits and no car at the end.

map.A loan only for businesses and big firms: A home loan whose payment stays the same for the term
map.A loan whose rate never changes for its: A loan used to pay for a car purchase

ww.A home loan whose payment stays the same: A loan with a payment that stays the same is a fixed-rate mortgage. An ARM resets its rate at set intervals based on a market index.
ww.A loan used to pay for a car purchase: A car loan finances a vehicle. An ARM is a home loan whose rate resets at set intervals based on a market index.

map.No need to repay any of the money you bo: Rates set by your credit score
map.Always higher interest rates than privat: Interest rates that vary by lender

ww.Rates set by your credit score: Federal student loan rates are set by Congress, not by credit score, though private lenders price loans by credit. Flexible repayment is the real benefit.
ww.Interest rates that vary by lender: Federal loan rates are set by Congress, not by each lender. The benefits are flexible repayment options and protections such as deferment.

map.Coverage for your own car repairs only,: Coverage for repairs to your own car after a crash
map.Coverage for theft only, and nothing els: Coverage for hail, fire and theft of your car

ww.Coverage for repairs to your own car aft: Repairs to your own car after a crash fall under collision coverage. Liability coverage pays for injuries and damage you cause to others.
ww.Coverage for hail, fire and theft of you: Hail, fire and theft fall under comprehensive coverage for your own car. Liability pays for injuries and property damage you cause to others.

map.Coverage for your own accidents only, no: Coverage for repairs to your car after your own crash
map.Coverage for rental cars only, on short: Coverage for damage you cause to another driver's car

ww.Coverage for repairs to your car after y: Repairs after your own crash are covered by collision coverage. Uninsured motorist coverage applies when another driver without insurance harms you.
ww.Coverage for damage you cause to another: Damage you cause to others is covered by liability coverage. Uninsured motorist coverage protects you when an uninsured driver causes the crash.

map.Coverage for cars only, and for nothing: Coverage for repairs to your own car
map.Coverage for rain damage only, when a st: Coverage for storm damage to your roof
map.Coverage for jewelry only, and not for o: Coverage for medical bills after an illness

ww.Coverage for repairs to your own car: Repairs to your own car fall under collision or comprehensive coverage. An umbrella policy adds liability protection beyond your other policies' limits.
ww.Coverage for storm damage to your roof: Storm damage to a roof is part of homeowners property coverage. An umbrella policy adds extra liability coverage, not property coverage.
ww.Coverage for medical bills after an illn: Medical bills are handled by health insurance. An umbrella policy adds extra liability coverage once other policy limits are used up.

map.Only by working at the company, which pa: Through fixed interest payments paid by the company
map.Only by borrowing money from the company: Through a salary paid by the company for owning stock
map.Only by paying a monthly fee to the stoc: Through rent collected from the company's buildings

ww.Through fixed interest payments paid by: Fixed interest payments go to bondholders who lend to the company. Stockholders earn through dividends and by selling shares at a higher price.
ww.Through a salary paid by the company for: Owning stock does not bring a salary. Stockholders earn through dividends from profits and by selling shares for more than they paid.
ww.Through rent collected from the company': Shareholders own part of the company and do not collect its rent. They earn through dividends and by selling shares at a higher price.

map.It guarantees the highest return in ever: It usually outperforms the market by a wide margin
map.It requires no money at all to buy share: It is insured by the government against losses

ww.It usually outperforms the market by a w: An index fund aims to match the market, not beat it. Its appeal is spreading risk across many companies at low cost.
ww.It is insured by the government against: Index funds are not government insured, and their value falls when the market falls. Their appeal is low cost and wide diversification.

map.A fund that holds one stock and never bu: A fund that moves toward riskier assets as the date nears
map.A fund that never changes its holdings f: A fund that holds a fixed 50-50 mix of stocks and bonds

ww.A fund that moves toward riskier assets: It is reversed. A target-date fund grows more conservative as the date nears, moving from stocks toward bonds and cash to reduce risk.
ww.A fund that holds a fixed 50-50 mix of s: A fixed mix is a balanced fund. A target-date fund changes its mix over time, becoming more conservative as the retirement date nears.

map.A stock issued only to children who cann: A stock of a large company paying steady dividends
map.A stock worth one cent forever and never: A stock whose price is set by the government

ww.A stock of a large company paying steady: Large established companies issue blue chip stocks. Penny stocks are low priced shares of small companies, often traded in thin markets.
ww.A stock whose price is set by the govern: Stock prices are set by buyers and sellers in the market, not by the government. A penny stock is a low priced share of a small company.

map.Prices never change at any time of the y: Sellers must honor the price you saw earlier
map.Waiting always makes the item cheaper to: Waiting lets you skip paying sales tax

ww.Sellers must honor the price you saw ear: Sellers can change prices at any time and are not bound to an earlier price. Waiting is useful because time shows whether you need the item.
ww.Waiting lets you skip paying sales tax: Sales tax applies whenever you buy, however long you wait. Waiting helps because time reveals whether you need the item.

map.A review that says Worst ever, with no r: A review written by someone who got the product free
map.A review that says Great!!! and nothing: A short review praising the brand but not the product
map.A review with no text at all, only a sta: A review that repeats the claims in the ad copy

ww.A review written by someone who got the: Reviews from people given free products may be biased toward praise. A detailed review explaining what worked and what did not is more trustworthy.
ww.A short review praising the brand but no: Praise for a brand name says little about the product's quality. A detailed review of what worked and what did not is more useful.
ww.A review that repeats the claims in the: Repeating ad claims adds no new information. A detailed review describing real use, strengths and flaws helps you judge the product.

map.A rate that applies only to cash advance: A rate that applies to balances after you miss a payment
map.A permanent low rate that never changes: A rate that applies when you take cash from an ATM

ww.A rate that applies to balances after yo: That describes a penalty APR, raised after missed payments. An introductory APR is a temporary low rate offered when you open a card.
ww.A rate that applies when you take cash f: Cash advances carry their own, usually higher APR. An introductory APR is a temporary low rate for new purchases or transfers.

map.Only the color of the card and its logo: How many reward points the card offers
map.Nothing, because 0% is permanent and nev: Nothing, since the rate is fixed by federal law
map.Only the name of the issuer printed on t: The number of stores that accept the card

ww.How many reward points the card offers: Reward points do not affect the cost of the 0% offer. You need to know when the promotional period ends and what regular APR then applies.
ww.Nothing, since the rate is fixed by fede: No federal law fixes a promotional rate. Introductory 0% offers are temporary, so you must check when they end and what the regular APR becomes.
ww.The number of stores that accept the car: Where a card is accepted has no bearing on the offer's cost. What matters is when the promotional period ends and the regular APR that follows.

map.Every month of each year: When your out-of-pocket maximum is reached

ww.On your birthday each year: Plans reset deductibles on the plan year, which may not match your birthday. It usually restarts on a set date such as January 1.
ww.When your out-of-pocket maximum is reach: Reaching the out-of-pocket maximum caps what you pay for the year but does not reset the deductible. It resets at the start of the next plan year.

map.A medicine that is always unsafe to take: A medicine that works differently from the brand-name drug but costs less
map.A medicine only for pets, made by vets a: A medicine sold without a prescription in drugstores and groceries

ww.A medicine that works differently from t: Generics must have the same active ingredient, strength and use as the brand-name drug. Their lower price comes from saved research and marketing costs.
ww.A medicine sold without a prescription i: Over the counter medicines are sold without a prescription. Generics are copies of brand-name drugs and many still require a prescription.

map.It makes premiums zero for everyone who: Insurers refund part of the premium to people who get checkups
map.It is always free everywhere in the whol: It replaces the need for a health insurance policy
map.It removes all medical risk for every pe: It lets people skip treatment when they get sick

ww.Insurers refund part of the premium to p: Insurers do not refund premiums for checkups. Preventive care saves money because catching problems early costs less than treating advanced illness.
ww.It replaces the need for a health insura: Preventive care does not replace insurance, which is still needed for illness, injury and hospital bills. It saves money by catching problems early.
ww.It lets people skip treatment when they: Checkups do not replace treatment when illness occurs. They save money by finding problems early, when care is simpler and cheaper.

map.Trading every day to chase small moves i: Switching funds each quarter to follow the latest trend
map.Buying only to resell right away for a q: Buying shares to sell once they rise a few percent

ww.Switching funds each quarter to follow t: Switching funds each quarter to follow trends is frequent trading. Long term investing means staying invested for years through market ups and downs.
ww.Buying shares to sell once they rise a f: Selling after a small gain is short-term trading. A long term investor keeps investments for years to benefit from growth and compounding.

map.It eliminates all of your risk: It makes returns easier to predict
map.It guarantees losses every year: It removes the need to research stocks
map.It always raises returns by a lot: It lets investors time the market with ease

ww.It makes returns easier to predict: Frequent trading adds timing errors and costs, which makes results less predictable. It hurts returns through fees and taxes.
ww.It removes the need to research stocks: Frequent trading raises the need for research and decisions. It hurts returns through commissions, spreads and higher taxes on short-term gains.
ww.It lets investors time the market with e: Few investors can time the market consistently, and trying adds costs. Fees and taxes from frequent trades reduce gains.

map.A deduction that must be itemized by eac: A deduction equal to the actual expenses you list on your return
map.A deduction only for businesses, claimed: A credit that reduces your tax bill dollar for dollar
map.A fee for filing a return that the IRS c: A refund the IRS sends when too much tax was withheld

ww.A deduction equal to the actual expenses: Listing actual expenses is itemizing. The standard deduction is a fixed amount most taxpayers subtract without listing expenses.
ww.A credit that reduces your tax bill doll: A credit cuts the tax owed directly, while a deduction lowers taxable income. The standard deduction is a fixed amount subtracted from income.
ww.A refund the IRS sends when too much tax: A refund returns tax withheld in excess of what you owe. The standard deduction is a fixed amount subtracted from income to lower taxable income.

map.Only the sticker price shown on the wind: The purchase price plus sales tax and fees
map.Only the monthly payment, the sole cost: The loan payments added up over the loan term
map.Only the cost of gas that the car burns: Fuel and maintenance costs for the first year

ww.The purchase price plus sales tax and fe: Price, tax and fees cover buying the car but not owning it. Total cost also includes insurance, fuel, maintenance, repairs and depreciation.
ww.The loan payments added up over the loan: Loan payments leave out insurance, fuel, maintenance and repairs. Total cost of ownership adds these running costs to the price of the car.
ww.Fuel and maintenance costs for the first: Fuel and maintenance cover just part of the running costs and ignore the purchase price. Total cost adds insurance, repairs and depreciation as well.

map.A fund that earns no interest at all for: A fund used to pay off debt faster with extra payments
map.A fund for emergencies only, not for pla: A fund kept for unexpected costs such as job loss
map.Money lost through bad investments and n: A retirement account that you draw from each month

ww.A fund used to pay off debt faster with: Paying off debt early is a debt repayment strategy. A sinking fund collects small amounts toward a known future cost.
ww.A fund kept for unexpected costs such as: Unexpected costs are covered by an emergency fund. A sinking fund is built for a known future expense, such as a vacation or insurance bill.
ww.A retirement account that you draw from: Drawing from a retirement account is a different goal. A sinking fund builds a savings amount before a known expense comes due.

map.It removes the need to budget at all in: It improves your credit score over time
map.It guarantees higher interest than any b: It stops inflation from reducing your savings

ww.It improves your credit score over time: Credit scores are based on borrowing and repayment history, not where savings are kept. A separate account helps by reducing the temptation to spend.
ww.It stops inflation from reducing your sa: Inflation affects the buying power of money in any account. Keeping savings apart helps by reducing the temptation to spend them.

map.Never using the card, so that no interes: Using a card with a low credit limit to restrict spending
map.Paying the full balance so that no inter: Moving a balance to a card with a zero rate for a year

ww.Using a card with a low credit limit to: A low limit restricts spending and is not a trap. The minimum payment trap occurs when you pay little each month and the balance lingers.
ww.Moving a balance to a card with a zero r: A balance transfer to a lower rate can reduce interest if paid down in time. The minimum payment trap comes from paying little each month.

map.A loan only for businesses that is repai: A loan for buying a home that is secured by the property
map.A gift from a bank to a customer that is: A credit line you borrow from and repay repeatedly up to a limit

ww.A loan for buying a home that is secured: A loan secured by a house is a mortgage. A personal loan is usually unsecured money borrowed for personal needs and repaid in installments.
ww.A credit line you borrow from and repay: Credit you can reuse up to a limit is revolving credit. A personal loan is a lump sum repaid in fixed installments.

map.You have no savings at all to cover the: You rely on credit cards to cover large costs
map.You want the highest possible premium ev: You want the lowest out-of-pocket cost on each claim

ww.You rely on credit cards to cover large: Depending on credit cards means you could not easily pay the deductible after a loss. A higher deductible suits someone with savings to cover it.
ww.You want the lowest out-of-pocket cost o: Wanting low out-of-pocket claim costs calls for a lower deductible. A higher deductible suits someone who has savings to cover the first costs.

map.A policy that pays only the item's depre: A policy that pays the price you originally paid for the item
map.A policy that pays nothing at all for lo: A policy that covers items bought within the past year

ww.A policy that pays the price you origina: Paying the original price ignores today's cost. Replacement cost policies pay what a new equivalent item costs at current prices.
ww.A policy that covers items bought within: Replacement cost coverage is not limited to recent purchases. It pays current prices to replace covered items after a covered loss.

map.It lowers your income tax to zero every: It lowers the fees charged on your investments
map.It guarantees investment gains every sin: It lets you skip contributing from your own pay

ww.It lowers the fees charged on your inves: A match is a contribution from the employer and does not change fund fees. Its value is the free money added to your retirement savings.
ww.It lets you skip contributing from your: A match typically depends on your own contributions, so skipping them forfeits the match. Taking full advantage means adding free money to your savings.

map.Holding only cash forever and never buyi: Holding shares in many companies in one industry
map.Holding only one type of asset for the w: Switching into whichever asset class gained most lately
map.Holding only your employer's stock for j: Holding several funds that all own the same stocks

ww.Holding shares in many companies in one: Shares in one industry still rise and fall together, so this is not spread across asset classes. Diversification mixes stocks, bonds, cash and other asset types.
ww.Switching into whichever asset class gai: Chasing recent winners concentrates money in one asset class. Diversification holds a mix of stocks, bonds, cash and others to cushion a single drop.
ww.Holding several funds that all own the s: Funds that own the same stocks give little spread of risk. Diversification mixes different asset classes such as stocks, bonds and cash.

map.No extra risk at all for the investor or: Higher taxes on the dividends the stock pays
map.Guaranteed high returns for the investor: Lower fees than a diversified fund would charge

ww.Higher taxes on the dividends the stock: Dividends are taxed the same whether the stock is the employer's or another company's. The extra risk is that job and savings depend on one company.
ww.Lower fees than a diversified fund would: Owning one stock does not cut risk, and fees are not the main issue. The extra risk is that both job and savings depend on one company.

map.No need to pay taxes on the income that: Paid sick leave and vacation from the client
map.Guaranteed steady income, as pay is the: A steady paycheck set by an employer

ww.Paid sick leave and vacation from the cl: Self-employed people usually get no paid leave from clients. The benefit is control over schedule and decisions, with less stable income.
ww.A steady paycheck set by an employer: A steady paycheck set by an employer comes with regular jobs. Self-employed income changes with customers and seasons; the benefit is control over schedule.

map.A cost that is zero in every single mont: A cost you plan for ahead, such as a holiday gift
map.A cost you pay every month on the first: A cost that stays the same on a regular schedule, like a loan payment

ww.A cost you plan for ahead, such as a hol: A cost you plan ahead for is a planned expense. An unplanned expense is a cost you did not expect or budget for.
ww.A cost that stays the same on a regular: A regular loan payment is a fixed expense that you plan for. An unplanned expense is a cost you did not see coming.

map.It always raises prices in the shop for: It charges members a fee each time they shop
map.It bans returns of any kind for all the: It lowers the quality of the goods the store sells

ww.It charges members a fee each time they: Most loyalty programs are free to join and do not charge per purchase. The real drawback is that rewards may tempt you to spend more than planned.
ww.It lowers the quality of the goods the s: Joining a loyalty program does not change product quality. The drawback is that the rewards may tempt members to spend more than planned.

map.Saving random amounts with no aim in min: Saving the same amount each month without a target
map.Never saving any money for any goal at a: Saving whenever the bank offers a sign-up bonus

ww.Saving the same amount each month withou: Saving without a target lacks the goal and date that define a goal-based plan. Goal-based saving sets specific amounts for specific goals by set dates.
ww.Saving whenever the bank offers a sign-u: Saving in response to bonuses is reactive and lacks target amounts or dates. A goal-based plan sets specific amounts for specific goals by set dates.

map.It never changes in value over time: It earns the highest interest rate available
map.It cannot be spent at all by anyone: It is insured by the federal government

ww.It earns the highest interest rate avail: Liquidity says nothing about the interest earned. It describes how quickly an asset can be turned into cash.
ww.It is insured by the federal government: Insurance protects deposits against bank failure, which is a separate idea. Liquid means an asset can be converted into cash quickly.

map.A gift of free goods that the seller han: A requirement to pay the full price in cash at the time of sale
map.A tax refund paid by the state to a pers: A discount the seller gives when you pay in cash on the spot
map.An interest-free loan that you never hav: A bank loan that is repaid in equal installments over several years

ww.A requirement to pay the full price in c: Paying in full at purchase is a cash sale. A deferred payment plan lets you take the goods now and pay later, sometimes with interest if late.
ww.A discount the seller gives when you pay: A cash discount rewards immediate payment. A deferred payment plan lets you buy now and pay later, sometimes with interest if the balance is not paid on time.
ww.A bank loan that is repaid in equal inst: Equal installments over years describe an installment loan from a lender. A deferred payment plan is a seller's offer to pay later, with interest if the balance is not paid on time.

map.A state where only the at-fault driver i: A state where the at-fault driver's insurer pays for injuries after a crash
map.A state where insurers never pay any cla: A state where drivers pay for their own injuries out of pocket

ww.A state where the at-fault driver's insu: That describes a traditional at-fault system, where the responsible driver's insurer pays. In no-fault states each driver's own insurer pays regardless of fault.
ww.A state where drivers pay for their own: No-fault states still require insurance. Each driver's own insurer pays their injury costs up to a set limit regardless of who caused the crash.

map.Buying only on margin with money borrowe: Borrowing from a broker to buy shares on margin
map.Buying and selling every day to gain fro: Buying shares and selling when the price jumps

ww.Borrowing from a broker to buy shares on: Buying on margin means borrowing from a broker, which adds risk. Buy and hold is about keeping investments, not borrowing to buy them.
ww.Buying shares and selling when the price: Selling as soon as the price jumps is short-term trading. Buy and hold means keeping investments through market ups and downs for long-term growth.

map.Plans never need any changes at all, eve: Savings accounts must be renewed with the bank
map.Banks require a new plan from every cust: Tax laws require savers to update their plans

ww.Savings accounts must be renewed with th: Savings accounts do not need renewal. Reviewing a plan is wise because income, costs and goals change over time.
ww.Tax laws require savers to update their: No law requires savers to update a plan. Reviews are a personal habit because income, costs and goals change over time.

map.A salary is only for part-time work, whi: A wage is paid in cash while a salary is paid by direct deposit
map.A wage is always higher than a salary, f: A salary pays extra for overtime hours while a wage covers regular hours

ww.A wage is paid in cash while a salary is: Both wages and salaries can be paid by cash, check or direct deposit. The difference is that wages are hourly and a salary is a fixed amount per pay period.
ww.A salary pays extra for overtime hours w: Overtime rules depend on the job, not on whether pay is a wage or a salary. A wage is paid by the hour and a salary is a fixed amount per pay period.

map.A mistake to hide from every employer th: A period without work; change your dates to cover it up
map.A reason never to apply, as employers hi: A period without work; avoid mentioning it in the interview
map.A required legal form that every worker: A written reference letter from your most recent employer

ww.A period without work; change your dates: Changing dates to hide a gap is dishonest and can cost you a job if discovered. A gap should be explained honestly and briefly.
ww.A period without work; avoid mentioning: Avoiding the topic looks evasive when employers notice the gap. Be honest and briefly explain what you did, such as study, caregiving or volunteering.
ww.A written reference letter from your mos: A reference letter is a recommendation from an employer. A resume gap is a period without paid work that you should explain honestly.

map.Refuse every interview that you are ever: Ask for a high starting pay in the interview
map.Apply with no contact details at all on: List her hobbies in detail on a long resume

ww.Ask for a high starting pay in the inter: Asking for high pay with no experience weakens her chances. Volunteering, building skills and preparing a clear resume show employers her value.
ww.List her hobbies in detail on a long res: A long list of hobbies buries relevant skills. A short, clear resume built on volunteering and skills is more convincing.

map.They replace warranties and stores' retu: They show the seller's profit on each sale
map.They are never needed for returns or for: They are required to pay the sales tax

ww.They show the seller's profit on each sa: Receipts record what you paid, not the seller's profit. Their value is proving a purchase for returns, warranties and budgeting.
ww.They are required to pay the sales tax: Sales tax is collected at the register whether or not you keep the receipt. Receipts help by proving a purchase for returns and warranties.

map.Pay the sticker price only, without disc: Ask a friend to buy the item for you at the posted price
map.Refuse to buy anything from the seller a: Accept the seller's first offer to finish the sale quickly

ww.Ask a friend to buy the item for you at: Having a friend buy at the posted price involves no discussion with the seller. Negotiating means talking with the seller to reach a lower or fair price.
ww.Accept the seller's first offer to finis: Accepting the first offer skips bargaining. Negotiating means discussing with the seller to reach a lower or fair price.

map.Older people never invest in the stock m: Young investors earn higher interest from banks
map.Retirement accounts are always fully ins: Young investors have lower investment fees

ww.Young investors earn higher interest fro: Banks pay rates based on the account, not the saver's age. A young investor can accept more risk because of more time to recover from declines.
ww.Young investors have lower investment fe: Fees depend on the funds and accounts chosen, not the investor's age. Young investors can take more risk because they have more time to recover from declines.

map.It means owning only one stock to focus: It means putting the whole portfolio in the best performing fund
map.It guarantees profits on every investmen: It raises the returns of each investment in the portfolio

ww.It means putting the whole portfolio in: Putting everything into one fund concentrates risk in one place. Diversification spreads money across investments so one poor performer matters less.
ww.It raises the returns of each investment: Diversification does not change how any one investment performs. It limits the damage when one performs poorly.

map.Stocks cannot be sold at any time or at: Stocks must be held for a year before they can be sold
map.Stocks always rise in six months, so the: Brokers charge a large penalty for selling within six months

ww.Stocks must be held for a year before th: Stocks can be sold on any trading day, with no required holding period. The risk is that prices may fall and force a sale at a loss.
ww.Brokers charge a large penalty for selli: Brokers do not charge penalties for selling within six months. The risk is that prices may fall, forcing a sale at a loss.

map.Reports never contain errors of any kind: Checking your own report lowers your credit score each time
map.Errors only help you and never cost you: Lenders are required to fix errors without being told

ww.Checking your own report lowers your cre: Checking your own report is a soft inquiry and does not lower your score. Checking matters because errors can lower your score and cost you money.
ww.Lenders are required to fix errors witho: Errors are corrected after you dispute them, not automatically. Checking your report lets you find mistakes that can lower your score and cost you money.

map.They are identical in every way and in e: Credit cards need a bank account and debit cards do not
map.Credit cards use only your cash and neve: Debit cards build a credit history and credit cards do not

ww.Credit cards need a bank account and deb: Debit cards draw from a bank account, so it is debit cards that need one. Credit cards borrow money from the issuer.
ww.Debit cards build a credit history and c: Credit card use is reported to the bureaus and builds credit history, while debit cards are not. Credit cards also borrow money; debit cards use your own funds.
